theme: Guard the Leader, But Do Your Own Job
hindi: दुर्योधन अपने सब सेनापतियों से कहता है: “आप सभी लोग सब मोर्चों पर अपने-अपने निश्चित स्थान पर डटे रहकर केवल भीष्म पितामह की ही सब ओर से रक्षा कीजिए।”
english: Duryodhana tells all his commanders: “Stand firm in your own places at every entrance and front, and be sure that all of you protect Bhishma above everything.”
deeper: After counting his warriors, Duryodhana gives an order. Everyone must stay at their assigned post, and everyone must guard Bhishma. Bhishma was the commander-in-chief, the leader whom the whole army looked up to. A good army does need to protect its leader, and standing in the right place is a sensible plan.

But listen to the feeling under the words. Duryodhana has just said that Bhishma guards the army (1.10). Now he asks the army to guard Bhishma. It sounds as if he is nervous. His whole hope rests on one person, and he is afraid of what will happen if that person is hurt. Fear often hides inside strong, loud orders.

For us, the verse is a gentle lesson. Teamwork means every person stays at their post and does their part well. But strength that rests on one person alone is shaky. Real confidence comes from a good cause, honest effort and a team that trusts each other, not from fear of losing one star.
words: at the entrances, positions or fronts
according to each one’s assigned share or division
background: The Kuru army and the Pandava army stand face to face at Kurukshetra. Duryodhana, the Kaurava prince, goes to his teacher Drona and describes the Pandava army (1.2). Then he names the great warriors on his own side: Drona, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama and others (1.8). He adds that many more brave fighters are ready to give their lives for him (1.9).

Next he compares the two armies. Ours is guarded by Bhishma, theirs by Bhima (1.10). The words can be read as “unlimited or not enough” and “limited or enough,” so his confidence and his worry are mixed together. In this verse he turns from talking to ordering. Every commander must hold the assigned position and protect Bhishma.
lessons: In a team, everyone has a place and a job, and the whole team gains when each person does theirs well.
It is wise to take care of your leaders, your helpers and your strengths.
If all your hope sits on a single person, the whole plan wobbles when that person is missing.
Sometimes strong orders come from a worried heart, so we should be gentle with ourselves and others when we feel afraid.
A good cause, honest effort and trust in each other give more safety than guarding one star.
examples: Aarav’s team has one great batsman, Kabir. Everyone keeps saying “Don’t let Kabir get out!” but the team also needs fielders, bowlers and other batters who play well.
Meera’s group has a topper, Ishaan. Instead of sharing the work, everyone leaves it all to him. A fair group gives each child a part to do.
On a school trip, Ritu is asked to count heads at the back of the bus and Dev at the front. Because each stays at their post, nobody is left behind.
Tanvi keeps telling her friend, “Please help me, only you can save me!” She is really afraid. Her real help is to revise a little herself each day.
Sandeep’s coach says, “Defenders, stay in your positions.” When every player holds their place, the team is safe even if the star forward is tired.
On Diwali, each cousin has a job: one makes rangoli, one arranges diyas and one serves sweets. Nobody tries to do everything, and nobody is idle.
Pranav always asks his elder brother to fight his battles with friends. Pranav grows braver when he learns to speak up kindly for himself.
Everyone keeps worrying about the lead actor forgetting his lines. The director smiles and says, “Let’s all learn our own lines well, so the play stands on all of us.”

story.title: Vikram and the Kabaddi Match
paras: In a village near Satara, the boys’ kabaddi team had reached the final. Their star raider was Vikram, quick as a sparrow. The captain, Sandeep, was nervous. Before the match he gathered everyone and said, “Forget everything else. Just protect Vikram. If Vikram is safe, we will win!”

In the first half, every boy ran around Vikram like a wall. Nobody guarded the corners, and nobody raided on his own. The other team noticed this. They simply ignored Vikram and attacked the empty corners, and they scored point after point.

At the break, Vikram said, “Sandeep bhaiya, I am happy that you care for me. But I cannot win alone. Let Pooja and Ravi guard the corners as you planned, and let Imran raid too. I will do my part and each of you will do yours.”

Sandeep took a deep breath. His worry had made him forget the plan. In the second half everyone went back to their own positions and trusted one another. The team won by two points, and they all cheered for each other, not only for Vikram.
story.moral: Lesson: Take care of your leaders and stars, but a team wins when everyone stands firm at their own post and trusts each other, not when it is afraid of losing one person.

quiz.q: What does Duryodhana ask his commanders to do in this verse?
o: Stay at their posts and protect Bhishma
Go and ask Krishna for help
quiz.x: He tells them to hold their assigned positions and guard Bhishma on all sides.

o: Everyone standing in their own assigned place
quiz.x: It means “according to each one’s share or division,” so each person keeps their own post.

quiz.q: What does Duryodhana’s order hint about his mind?
o: He is worried and depends heavily on one person
quiz.x: Asking everyone to guard Bhishma shows that he fears losing the one leader his hopes rest on.

quiz.q: What is the best lesson for us from this verse?
o: Let one star do all the work
Do your own part well and don’t depend on one person alone
quiz.x: Teamwork means each person does their part, and a team is stronger when it doesn’t depend on a single star.

reel.hook: Why was Duryodhana so afraid, even with a huge army?
reel.lesson: Do your own part well, and never rest all your hopes on one person.
reel.caption:
Duryodhana asked everyone to guard just one person. Does that sound like confidence, or worry? 🤔
A team is strong when everyone does their own part, not when it leans on one star. 🛡️
Who is on your team today?
